discovery.hypothesis: Pastrnak had 4 or more shots on goal in three straight games and has 61 shots this season, close to double any other Bruin. With Hagens on injured reserve, he may carry even more of the offense. Florida ranks near the bottom of the league in blocked shots.
discovery.question: Can Pastrnak clear 3.5 against a Florida team that allows only 24.6 shots per game, the third-fewest in the league? And is the 3.5 line still available, or has it moved toward the 2.5 that one book listed?

assessment.reason: The projected mean is about 3.2 shots with a median of 3, below the 3.5 line. Even the upper sensitivity bound stays short of the +115 break-even.
assessment.model_case: Recent four-shot games support heavy volume, but the projection for about 19.6 minutes lands under 3.5. Florida reportedly allows few shots, which would cut against the over rather than for it.
assessment.price_case: This is the 3.5 line at +115, needing a win chance in the mid-forties. Four other books are near this quote. The withheld forecast and the minimum odds of roughly +215 sit far from this price.
assessment.context_case: The injury snapshot does not list Pastrnak, but that does not establish he is active. The Hagens injured-reserve claim is unsourced here. Line and power-play roles remain unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: A larger shooting share with teammates out, plus a likely Boston territorial edge against a tired Florida team, could push volume past four. The recent three-game streak shows the ceiling is real.

findings.note: NHL.com lists Barkov, Marchand, Lundell and Vilmanis as injured for Florida and Swayman projected for Boston. The Bruins are without Hagens (back, out a couple of weeks) and Poitras, and Eyssimont was recalled to play.

Two Covers analyst picks back Boston on the moneyline, one saying to play it up to 59%, citing Florida's back-to-back and missing forwards. On the other side, the same page says Florida is very stingy on shots and has won 5 of its last 6 games in Boston.

Florida played in Washington on Saturday (Schmid lost 4-3), so this is a back-to-back. The likely starter, Markstrom, has given up 3+ goals in his last two starts with an .885 save percentage this season.

Covers lists trends that lean Over: the Over is 4-0-1 in Florida's last 5 games and 5-0 in its last 5 against Atlantic teams. The same page lists the Panthers total at U5.5 (-105), so other books may have a lower total than 6.5.

NHL.com projects Swayman and Markstrom to start in goal. Florida will be without Barkov, Marchand, Lundell (day to day) and Vilmanis, and Boston will be without Hagens and Poitras. Florida played Saturday, so this is a back-to-back.

Covers analyst Chris Faria put Under 6.5 in a parlay, citing strong defense from both teams. The page also says Markstrom has a .885 SV% and has allowed 3+ goals in three straight starts, and that the Over is 5-0-1 in Boston's last 6 games as a favorite.
